hints: Notice the incident light is already vertically polarised and the filter transmission axis is at $30^{\circ}$ to the vertical, so $\theta = 30^{\circ}$ is the angle in Malus law.
Recall that the transmitted electric field amplitude is the component $E_0 \cos\theta$ along the transmission axis, while intensity is proportional to amplitude squared.
walkthrough: Identify the given values: incident intensity $I_0 = 24\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ of vertically polarised light, and angle between polarisation direction and transmission axis $\theta = 30^{\circ}$.
State the governing rule for polarised light through a polariser, Malus law: $I = I_0 \cos^2\theta$.
Substitute with units: $I = 24\ \text{W m}^{-2} \times 0.75 = 18\ \text{W m}^{-2}$, which is less than $I_0$ as expected.

options.B: This value is close to $24 \cos 30^{\circ}$ and omits the squaring of the transmitted amplitude to get intensity.
options.C: Intensity cannot increase from $24\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ to a larger value when part of the wave is absorbed by the filter.
options.D: Intensity cannot increase from $24\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ to a larger value when only the $30^{\circ}$ component is transmitted.
